## Body

# #344 review at e56bcb4: pass-with-notes

Single round (C34). Correctness, cost, security, privacy. No blockers.

## 1. Authority unchanged (holds)
- Authority still comes only from `seat_role_for(role id)` (holders.rs, untouched) and `require_prime` (project prime_id or seat.role == prime, untouched). No permission or SeatRole code is in the diff.
- `meta.type` / `role_type` is read in five places, all display-only: `seat_type()` (list TYPE), view rows `type`/`type_suggestion`, the `two_types` action, `retype_plan`, and `check_role` (validates the document's own shape). Nothing branches on a type to grant, refuse or route.
- A role added with `--type prime|pa|project-manager` grants nothing; retype only writes `meta.type` + changelog. The test `the_list_and_the_view_show_each_seats_type` asserts the holder stays `role: worker`.
- `seed` and `retype --apply` are ungated like `add`/`edit` today (same model). `seed`'s path is `community/seeds/<type>.md` after `types::get` validates the type, so no traversal.

## 2. Migration 0052 (holds)
- `ALTER TABLE community_pointers ADD COLUMN role_type TEXT` (nullable); `user_version` and `SCHEMA_VERSION` both go to 52; pr-freeze FINAL reports it above main's highest. Upsert sets the column; `rebuild` recomputes it from the branch head (`from_branch_head`); the test proves a stale stamp is repaired by rebuild.
- A stale stamp feeds only `open_holding_types` → `pij list` TYPE/types. The view and two-types action read the documents themselves. Nothing else reads it.

## 3. Behaviour change (holds, one note)
- E-RS-TYPE-MISSING lists the ten and names `--type` and `pij directory types <type>`. `--kind`/`--lifecycle` (flag or `--set`) are ignored with `warnings`. The schema keeps `kind`/`lifecycle` optional, so old docs validate; `edit` of an untyped role passes `require=false`.

## 4. Retype (holds)
- Dry-run by default (test: head unchanged). `--apply` needs `--why`, re-plans under the writer's lock, writes only `Decided` (template table, then id pattern, then re-checked with `check_role`). Skips typed or retired roles. A second `--apply` is a no-op (test).

## 5. JSON (holds)
- `SeatProjection` adds `type` (null when none) and `types`. `SeatDescriptor`/`SeatSize` have no `type`/`types` key, so the flatten has no collision. View rows add `type`/`type_suggestion` and keep `kind`. Rust and TS render the same golden; nothing is removed or renamed.

## 6. Cost (holds, one note)
- One SQLite query per `/v1/seats` request: `INDEXED BY community_assignments_open_by_seat` (partial, `to_at IS NULL`, matches the WHERE) joined on the pointers primary key (project, path). It is one query, not a query per seat. No launch, loop, timer or hook. `types` reads compiled-in bytes. `role_type_at` is one in-process file read for each written path, on the write path only. No new launch site.

## 7. Mutation checks (git archive HEAD into a mktemp dir; `just shared-build`, nice 19)

- `rule.fixed && false` → `a_default_rule_changes_with_a_reason_and_a_fixed_one_never` FAILED

## 8. Privacy (clean)
Searched the added lines for home paths, names, emails, company and machine paths. Only hit: the existing placeholder `/home/someone/.claude-alt` in the list golden. The seeds and type definitions are clean.

## Notes (P3, non-blocking; the author may take any)
- N1 refusal hint: E-RS-TYPE-MISSING's next line names only `add <id> --type`. It does not mention `--from template:<name>` (which also satisfies it) or `pij directory retype` for existing roles. The same hint shows on the edit path (`edit --file` dropping the type) and still says `add`.
- N2 cost row wording: the PR says "one per pij list call". `/v1/seats` is also polled by federation fan-in (`/v1/seats?scope=local`, 1 s per peer by default) and the extension roster, so the query rides those polls too. It is still cheap (indexed, in-process, no launch, not per seat), but the row should say so.
- N3 unvalidated stamp: `role_type_at` / `of_role` take any string from a hand-edited role document, and `pij list` prints it raw. `types::get(t).is_ok()` in `role_type_at` would keep a junk or escape-laden value out of the store. A brake only: dropping it shows `-`.
- N4 label vs authority: TYPE prefers the held roles' type over the seat role. A prime or pm seat that holds a coder role shows `coder`, and a worker holding a role typed `prime` shows `prime`. That matches "one label = its type", but readers must not take TYPE as authority. A line in pij-rs-api.md saying so would help.
- N5 an edit of an untyped role with `--type-change` writes `type_changes` unchecked, because `check_role` returns early with no type. Harmless until it is typed, when the next edit re-checks it.
- N6 retype's id prefixes (`qa*`, `security*`, `coder*`, `reviewer*`) can over-match, for example `qanat` becomes reviewer. That conflicts a little with "--apply writes only what it is sure of"; prefix plus `-` or an exact match would be safer.
